column2: Then you are indeed our maker; all good dwellings for us, songs rich in strength and wealth.
Agni, come with the fires; we choose you as priest; let the ready, offering-laden grass anoint you, the best sacrificer, to sit.
To you, son of strength, Angiras, the ladles go at the sacrifice; we ask Agni, grandson of strength, ghee-haired, first at sacrifices.
Let our songs go to the sharp-flamed, the beautiful; let the sacrifices go with homage to the much-wealthy, much-praised, for help.
Agni, son of strength, Jatavedas, to give desirable things; who became twofold, immortal among mortals, the most joyful priest among the people.
The unconquerable leader of the human clans, Agni — a swift chariot, ever new.
The giving mortal obtains offerings and the dwelling of the pure-flamed by the carrier.
Overcomer of all attackers, unharmed wisdom of the gods, Agni, most famous.
Make your mind auspicious in the Vritra-battle, by which you overcame in battles; break the firm ones, many who strive; we would serve you for your help.
O Agni, lord of cattle-rich strength, son of might, give us, Jatavedas, great fame.
Kindled, the Vasu, the seer, Agni, praised with song, shine richly for us, O of many forms.
O king, by night and by day, Agni, you yourself, O sharp-jawed, burn the demons in turn.
Desiring strength I praise Agni, the beloved guest of every clan, your door-guard, with the thoughts of the strong.
Whom the people with offerings praise with praises like Mitra, like the ghee-sprinkler.
The most praised Jatavedas, who with raised offerings at the gods' service sent the oblations to heaven.
I praise Agni kindled with the kindling-stick, with song, the pure purifier, firm before the sacrifice; the sage, priest, much-chosen, guileless, the seer; with favors we ask Jatavedas.
You, Agni, messenger, immortal, in every age they set as carrier of oblations, protector, to be praised; both gods and mortals have sat with homage by the wakeful, all-pervading lord of the clans.
Adorning both ways according to the laws, you go, messenger of the gods, between the two worlds; when we choose your thought and favor, then be for us a threefold shelter, kind.
Whose threefold, uncovered grass stood unwithering; even the waters placed a step.
The step of the bountiful god, with unassailable helps; auspicious, like the sun in sight.
For this Indra grew in manly strength, in the joy of the soma pressed in Vishnu; today the Ayus praise his greatness as before.
The singers, knowing the leading, offer you hymns; Indra and Agni, I choose strength.
Indra and Agni, you shook ninety forts of the Dasa-wives with one deed together.
Indra and Agni, the thoughts go forth to your works, along the paths of truth.
Indra and Agni, your strengths, seats and strengthening offerings are set for the winning of water.
The fountain of the horse of Puru, maker of many, of the cows, O golden god; no one hinders the gift when I ask; bring it then.
You come to the wanderer; find fortune for the winning of wealth; rise up, bounteous one, for the seeking of cattle, Indra, for the seeking of horses.
You, much, thousands and hundreds, give herds; we have made Indra the Purandara with wise words, singing for help.
Like a horse by songs, the chariot, the good givers are adorned, god-seeking; protect both children and grandchildren, O wondrous lord of the clans, for you bring the bounty of the bounteous.
Hear this my call, Varuna, and today be gracious; seeking help I have turned to you.
With what help, bull, do you delight in us? With what do you bring to the singers?
Indra by greatness spread both worlds, strength; Indra made the Sun shine; in Indra all the worlds are restrained; in Indra the pressed drops.
O Vishvakarman, strengthened by the offering, sacrifice yourself, for your body is your own; let others be bewildered all around; here may our bounteous one be the patron.

He guards after the eastern direction, knowing; he strives with the rays, a beautiful chariot, a beautiful divine chariot. The hymns have come with manly strength; delight Indra for victory. When you two are the thunderbolt unshaken and unshaken in battles.

You indeed found the wealth of the Panis; you cleanse it with your mothers in your own home, in the house with the thoughts of truth. Like a Saman from afar, where the thoughts delight; with three-substance ruddy ones I place vigor; shining, I place vigor.
And for us thought that gains cattle, horses and strength — make it manful, for help.
Of the man who labors, the sweat of true strength — know the desire of the longing one.
May the sons hear our songs near, those of immortality; may they be most gracious to us.
We bring forth great praise to you two, heaven and earth, pure, for glorification.
Purifying each other with your own skill, you two rule; you carry eternal truth.
You two accomplish the great one of Mitra, crossing and filling truth; sit around the sacrifice.
A hymn to the lord of bounties, O song-carried hero, whose is the might; let it be a pleasant offering.
Stand up for our help, hundred-powered, in this contest; we shall speak together among others.
Honey has been poured out in the lotus toward the pit-like cloud, at the release of the well.
They pour with homage the well with its high wheel, all-moving, with its lower door unfailing.
May we not fear, may we not tire, in friendship with your fierce self; great is your visible deed, bull; may we see Turvasha and Yadu.
To the left side you cover; his gift does not vex, like a bull's; the cows mixed with honey and bee-juice — come quickly, run, drink.
This thousandfold one, made strong by the sages, has spread like the ocean; true is his greatness; I praise his strength at the sacrifices, in the kingdom of sages.
Whose all this Aryan, Dasa, treasure-guarding enemy is; across the ruddy one, the lamp, to you alone this wealth is anointed.
The hasteners, the sages, have sung the honeyed ghee-dripping hymn; wealth has spread to us, manly strength, to us the sounding drops.
Be to us, lord of the bay horses, O drop, most divine in pleasure; like a friend to a friend, a leader, be for splendor.
You from of old, from us, drive away any godless devourer; overcoming, drop, drive off the oppressors and the double-minded.
They anoint, they adorn, they decorate; they lick the skill, they anoint with honey; at the breath of the river, the golden-purified take the bull flying in the waters.
Sing to the wise, flowing one; the drink flows like a great stream; like a snake creeping, it moves in its skin; like a horse in play the bay bull has run.

The king, foremost, to be praised in the waters, is strengthened; the measurer of days is set in the worlds; the bay, ghee-dropping, fair-faced ocean with light-chariot flows for wealth, a home-dweller.
With all fires, Agni, to this sacrifice and this word, grant us, O son of strength, joy.
Whatever we sacrifice to god after god in the eternal course, in you alone the offering is poured.
May the lord of the clans, the joyful, choice priest, be dear to us; may we be dear, with good fires.
We call Indra from all sides for the people; may he be ours alone.
O bull, you, the giver of food, increase the waters and this pot for us, unrepelled.
Like a bull among the herds, a lord who wanders, he drives the peoples by might, ruling, unrepelled.
You save children and grandchildren with the unharmed, untiring protectors; Agni, drive away the divine anger and the godless forces from us.
What is that name of yours, Vishnu, that you observe, when you declare "I am Shipivishta"? Do not hide from us this form, which you took in another shape in the battle.
Today I proclaim that offering for you, O Shipivishta, knowing the ways; I praise you, the strong, who dwell at the far end of this space.
I make the vashat for you, Vishnu; accept my offering, O Shipivishta; may the good praises strengthen you; protect us always with blessings.
O Vayu, I come with bright soma to you, the first of the honey, at the heavenly worship; come to drink the soma, desirable god with your team.
Indra and Vayu, you deserve the drinking of these somas; for the drops go to you both, as waters flow down together.
Vayu and Indra, strong, with one chariot, lords of strength, with your teams, come for help to drink the soma.
Then, adorned at night, he plunges into strengths when the thoughts of Vivasvat urge the bay one to go.
We cleanse his exhilaration, which is best drunk by Indra, which the cows with their mouths and the sages set before and now.
They praised him, being purified, with an ancient song; and the thoughts, bearing the name of the gods, arranged.
May that son of ours, wide-going, kindly, generous, be strong.
Protect us always from the mortal who intends evil, from far and near, you, all-living.
Both worlds followed your speeding might, like mothers a child; all your enemies were broken at your wrath, when you, Indra, overcame Vritra.
In the exhilaration of soma he crossed the air and the lights, when Indra split Vala.
He drove out the cows for the Angirases, revealing those hidden in the cave; he drove the nearest Vala.
The warrior, tireless, soma-drinker, unshaken, the man of irresistible skill.
Teach us, Indra, to wealth, knowing much, O praised with hymns; protect us in the farther gain.
Yours is that great power, Indra; yours the skill and wisdom; the thought sharpens the choice thunderbolt.
Heaven, Indra, increases your manliness, earth your fame; the waters and mountains impel you.
Vishnu of great dwelling, Mitra, Varuna praise you; the Marut host exults after you.
Surely, Agni, you will bring us wealth for the seeking of cattle; make wide, make wide for us.
Agni, do not leave us in the great battle like a burden-bearer; win us the combined wealth.
With the strong one he split the head of the quivering Vritra with the hundred-jointed thunderbolt.
His might shone when he turned both, Indra, heaven and earth like a skin.
Well-minded, wealthy, delightful, kind.
Come, bull of the same form; these two good yoke-bearers draw near to them.
The heads are bowed; in the middle of the water stands the gracious one, pointing with ten horns.
Come here, two prayer-yoked bay horses carrying the friend, Indra, who loves songs, with songs.
The drinker, Vritra-slayer, comes to the pressed soma, far from us; the hundred-helper holds back.
You have expanded, bull, by greatness, to enjoy the soma of the wakeful, which is, Indra, in your belly.
Let soma be enough for your belly, Vritra-slayer; the drops enough for the abodes.
May the great, immeasurable, smoke-bannered, much-shining one urge us for thought and strength.
May the lord of the clans, the divine banner, like a wealthy man, hear us; with hymns Agni of great light.
The Vasu does not withhold the gift of cattle-rich strength when he hears the songs.
Quickly the Dasyu-slayer indeed goes to the cattle-rich pen; with his powers may he protect us.
Vishnu, the unconquerable guardian, strode three steps, upholding laws thereby.
Behold the deeds of Vishnu, by which he touched the vows, the fit friend of Indra.
That highest step of Vishnu the seers always behold, like an eye spread in heaven.
That, the sages, the wakeful, kindle together — the highest step of Vishnu.
From where Vishnu strode, from there may the gods protect us, on the earth's summit.
Let not the ritual priests keep you from us far away; come to our shared feast from near or far, and listen here.
These prayer-makers sit together at the honey, like flies at the pressing; the singers, desiring wealth, place their desire in Indra as the foot upon the chariot.
An ancient thought has been praised; speak a prayer for Indra; they have sung the great ones of truth; the singer's wisdom has been released.
Indra shook the great riches together, earth and Sun; the bright pure somas mixed with milk delighted Indra.
For Indra to drink, Soma, you are poured around for the Vritra-slayer, for the man, the giver of gifts, the god sitting in the seat.
Friends, may we, the singers, attain that very radiant one, and win strength-giving wealth.
What mortal, O Indra, dares to withstand you, Vasu? Faith in you, bounteous, in the farther heaven, the strong man wins strength.
Urge the bounteous in the Vritra-slayings, those who give dear wealth; by your guidance, bay-horsed one, with the patrons, may we cross all evils.
O Indra, stander on the bay horses, none reaches your ancient praise; none rejoices with might.
We call him, lord of strengths, seeking fame, with ungrudging offerings, to be strengthened.
Praise Agni, giver of abundant bounty, O sage, of wondrous flame, the restrainer; at this rite of Soma, Sobhari, bring forth the first one for the sacrifice.
Come, Soma, sounding with the stones across the sheep's wool; like a man entering a city, the bay one enters the vessels, dwelling in the woods.
He is cleansed across the fine fleeces, the ram, the bountiful, like a horse seeking strength; to be rejoiced in, flowing, with the wise, Soma with the sages.
We have indeed fed this thunderbolt-bearer here; today at the pressing bring the soma for him; honor now the famed one.
Even the wolf, at his barrier, adorns the wise among the observant; accepting this hymn of ours, come, Indra, with a wondrous thought.
Indra and Agni, you adorn the lights of heaven in battles; that heroism of yours is known.
Indra and Agni, the thoughts go forth to your works, along the paths of truth.
Indra and Agni, your strengths, seats and strengthening offerings are set for the winning of water.
Who knows him, drinking with us at the pressing? What strength has he won? He who, delighted by the soma-drink of the fair-jawed, breaks the forts with might.
Like a wild beast driven by gifts, you place your movement in many places; none restrains you at the pressing; great, you move by might.
He who is fierce, unfallen, firm, prepared for battle; if the bounteous one hears the call of the singer, Indra does not neglect, but comes.
The flowing somas have been released, the bright drops, toward all poetry.
The flowing ones have been released from heaven and from the air, on the summit of the earth.
The swift flowing, bright drops have been released, smiting all enemies.
I call the swift, Vritra-slaying, victorious, unconquered ones, best winners of strength, Indra and Agni.
The singers, knowing the leading, offer you hymns; Indra and Agni, I choose strength.
Indra and Agni, you shook ninety forts of the Dasa-wives with one deed together.
We approach you, of pleasing sight, O born of strength, with offerings; Agni, we send songs.
We have come to your shelter like shade from heat, O Agni, golden-seen.
